subject: Oceanography
title: Bioluminescence
description: A fast breakdown of Bioluminescence for builders.

hook.text: In the deep sea, 90% of animals produce their own light—the dark ocean glows with living lanterns.

buildup.text: Bioluminescence uses a chemical reaction—luciferin reacts with oxygen to produce cold light.

discovery.text: Animals use it for hunting (anglerfish lures), defense (squid ink decoys), and communication (mating flashes).

twist.text: Some fish use counterillumination—matching their belly glow to surface light to hide their silhouette.

climax.text: The total light produced by deep-sea organisms exceeds that of all visible stars combined—it's just hidden.

punchline.text: The darkest place on Earth is actually full of light.

quiz.question: What percentage of deep-sea animals produce bioluminescence?
